evidence.note: tk /tok-/ “midst, (toward) the midst (of)”; btk “in the midst (of)”; compared there with Hebrew תָּוֶךְ, construct תּוֹךְ.
tk /tok-/ < *tawk “(in the) midst (of)”, derived from a triconsonantal root.
“b- + words for ‘midst’: bqrb, btk ‘in the midst of’.”

cognates.gloss: midst, (toward) the midst of; btk “in the midst of”
cognates.note: The same noun used as a preposition, alone and with b- (btk), as Hebrew uses תּוֹךְ and בְּתוֹךְ. The grammar gives it as /tok-/ from *tawk, and pairs btk with bqrb “in the midst of”, as Hebrew pairs בְּתוֹךְ with בְּקֶרֶב.

evidence.note: “n.f. MIDST”, cf. Hebrew tok; KAI 24.5/6 (Kilamuwa), bt ʾby bmtkt mlkm ʾdrm, “My royal house was in the midst of those of more powerful kings”.

cognates.note: A feminine noun with prefixed m- on the same t-k base, in the phrase bmtkt “in the midst of”, the Phoenician counterpart of בְּתוֹךְ.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh's purpose for the sanctuary is stated in this word: “they shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst” (Exo 25:8); he brought Israel out of Egypt “to dwell in their midst” (Exo 29:45–46), and promised, “I will walk in your midst and be your God, and you shall be my people” (Lev 26:11–12). Because he dwelt in their midst, the camp and the land were to be kept clean (Num 5:3; 35:34). The prophets carry the promise forward to the land and the city: “I will set my sanctuary in their midst forever”, and the nations will know it (Ezk 37:26–28); the temple is “the place of my throne … where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever” (Ezk 43:7, 9); “I will return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem” (Zec 8:3), and many nations will join themselves to Yahweh in that day (Zec 2:14–15). Paul applies Lev 26:12 to the believers, “you are the temple of the living God, as God said, I will dwell in them and walk among them” (2Co 6:16). From the verses: God's dwelling among men is promised on the earth, his throne set in the midst of Israel at Jerusalem with the nations joined to him; until then those he calls are his temple, among whom he walks.

Those Yahweh dwells among are called out of the midst of what is unclean. Moses told Israel, “separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation” (Num 16:21); Isaiah, “go out from her midst, purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of Yahweh” (Isa 52:11); Jeremiah, “flee from the midst of Babylon … go out from her midst, my people” (Jer 51:6, 45). Paul joins Isa 52:11 to the promise of Lev 26:12: “come out from their midst and be separate, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you, and you will be a Father to you” (2Co 6:16–18), and the voice from heaven repeats Jeremiah's call over Babylon the great: “come out of her, my people” (Rev 18:4). From the verses: the son stands in the midst of the congregation, and those who are God's separate themselves from that which he will judge.

In Psalm 22 the sufferer, after his deliverance, says: “I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly (בְּתוֹךְ קָהָל) I will praise you” (Psa 22:23). Hebrews puts these words in the mouth of Jesus: “I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the ecclesia (ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας) I will sing your praise” (Heb 2:12), because “he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one”, and so “he is not ashamed to call them brothers” (Heb 2:11). He shared their flesh and blood, and “had to be made like his brothers in all things” (Heb 2:14, 17). From the verses: the son stands in the midst of the ecclesia as one of the brothers, a man of their nature, praising his God and theirs.

note: Root key: תוכ. BDB files תָּוֶךְ and תִּיכוֹן under תוה beside unrelated words, and the database keys these words' tokens with root תוה (word_info) and entry_root תוה for w.aj.ae and w.aj.af; the root table has a תוכ row, but its four forms are parses of other roots (הַמְתֻכָּן, לֶכְתֵּךְ, וְהִתַּכְתִּי, לְוָתָךְ). תוכ is chosen as the word's own consonants, as כי and אמ were chosen for ki.json and im.json, so that the root key תוה stays free for an entry on תָּו “mark” and its verb. No other entry has root תוכ. Because the tokens are keyed תוה, the app finds this entry through haqor_lexicon_bdb and entry_root (bdb keys w.aj.ae, w.aj.af); if a later entry takes root תוה, the lookup by root would send these tokens to that entry first, and the join should then be checked. Words: w.aj.ae (תָּוֶךְ) and w.aj.af (תִּיכוֹן); w.an.af is a cross-reference with no tokens. Left for an entry of their own (they share only BDB's page): תָּו “mark” (w.ai.ab, Ezk 9:4, 6; Job 31:35), the verb תָּוָה “make a mark” (w.ai.ad, Ezk 9:4), תַּאֲוָה (w.ai.ac; its 9 tokens are the “desire” word of אוה filed here by spelling, Gen 49:26 apart), תָּוָה “pain” (w.aj.aa, Psa 78:41), תּוֹלָל (w.aj.ak, Psa 137:3), Aramaic תְּוַהּ “be startled” (xw.ac.aa, Dan 3:24), and the name תּוֹחַ / תֹּחוּ (w.aj.ab, w.am.ad), a place apart because its consonants differ (ח); no name is formed from תוכ, so no name entry. The place חֲצַר הַתִּיכוֹן (Ezk 47:16) is a place name. Uses: w.aj.ae counts 419 tokens by spelling; Psa 72:14 מִתּוֹךְ is תֹּךְ “oppression” (root תככ, w.ap.ab; parallel חָמָס), so the word's own count is 418. No Aramaic word: Biblical Aramaic and the Peshitta say “in the midst” with גּוֹא / ܓܘ (root גו), another word; SEDRA has no root tk. Cognates not found: no Arabic cognate in Lane (تك and تيك are unrelated), none in Oracc's Akkadian (Akkadian “midst” is qablu, qerbu), nothing in Anderson–Moser. Leads not followed: DULAT for the fuller Ugaritic attestation; Krahmalkov's TKT (p. 490, “?etym.”, an object in the temple, KAI 10.5 btkt ʾbn), which some read as “midst”, is not cited because he gives no etymology; Old Aramaic and Moabite for a t-k word (DNWSI not vendored). Krahmalkov's p. 319 and Segert's pp. 78, 102, 203 are from the text layers' running heads; check against the scans. Greek: μέσος is given on תָּוֶךְ only; the Septuagint renders תִּיכוֹן by μέσος too (Exo 26:28; Jdg 7:19; 1Ki 6:6, 8) but no New Testament verse quotes those, so no Greek is listed for it. Lev 26:11–12 is rendered ἐν ὑμῖν, not with μέσος, so 2Co 6:16 is cited in the sense and the doctrine, not under μέσος. Senses are illustrative, not exhaustive (418 uses); many verses could stand under “among” or “inside” alike.
summary: תָּוֶךְ is the middle of a thing and the inside of it: the tree of life stood “in the middle of the garden” (Gen 2:9), the city “in the middle” of its pasturelands with two thousand cubits on every side (Num 35:5). Nearly always it is joined to a preposition: בְּתוֹךְ “in the midst of, among, within”, מִתּוֹךְ “out of the midst of, from among”, אֶל־תּוֹךְ “into”. Yahweh made Israel a sanctuary “that I may dwell in their midst” (Exo 25:8), spoke to them “from the midst of the fire” (Deu 4:12), and promises to dwell “in the midst of the sons of Israel forever” (Ezk 43:7); the adjective תִּיכוֹן is the middle one of three. Ugaritic tk, btk and Phoenician mtkt “midst” are the same word.

evidence.locator: Gen.2.9, בְּתוֹךְ → ἐν μέσῳ; Psa.22.23, בְּתוֹךְ קָהָל → ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας; Isa.52.11, מִתּוֹכָהּ → ἐκ μέσου αὐτῆς; μέσος renders תָּוֶךְ ×278

evidence.note: Psa 22:23 quoted: “I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the ecclesia (ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας) I will sing your praise.”
Isa 52:11 quoted: “Come out from their midst (ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν) and be separate.”
“The tree of life, which is in the midst (ἐν μέσῳ) of the paradise of God”: the tree of Gen 2:9.

greek.gloss: middle; ἐν μέσῳ “in the midst”, ἐκ μέσου “out of the midst”

senses.definition: The middle of a thing or place, with something on either side. Where the text gives equal distances on each side, it denotes the centre.

evidence.note: Two thousand cubits are measured on the east, south, west and north, וְהָעִיר בַּתָּוֶךְ, “and the city in the middle”.
Abram cut the animals בַּתָּוֶךְ, “in the middle”, and laid each half opposite the other.
Samson took hold of עַמּוּדֵי הַתָּוֶךְ, “the pillars of the middle”, on which the house stood, one with his right hand and one with his left.
After עֵץ הַחַיִּים, “the tree of life”, בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן locates the tree “in the middle of the garden”. The prefix בְּ supplies “in”, and הַגָּן completes the construct תוֹךְ, “the middle of”.
The expanse stands בְּתוֹךְ הַמָּיִם, “in the midst of the waters”. Its task of separating waters from waters places water on either side of it.
One torch between two tails, בַּתָּוֶךְ, “in the middle”.
Israel went into the middle of the sea on dry ground, the waters a wall on their right and on their left.
The priests stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan.
The opening for the head “in the middle of” the robe.
The middle bar runs “in the middle of” the frames from end to end.
“And the city in its midst”: in the middle of the strip of land set apart for it; also Ezk 48:8, the sanctuary in the middle of the contribution.

senses.definition: With a group of people or things: one of them, or set in their middle, so that the group is around him.

evidence.note: “The Levites were not counted in the midst of the sons of Israel”: not numbered as one of the tribes.
Zelophehad's daughters: “Give us a possession in the midst of the brothers of our father”, a share as one of them.
“This is Jerusalem: in the midst of the nations I have set her, and lands are all around her.”
Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth.
“You are a prince of God among us.”
Aaron has no portion among Israel: “I am your portion and your inheritance in the midst of the sons of Israel.”
Job gave his daughters an inheritance in the midst of their brothers; also Pro 17:2.
Saul stood in the midst of the people, taller than all of them.
The Shunammite: “I dwell in the midst of my people.”
“I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips.”
The sons of God came to present themselves before Yahweh, “and the adversary also came in their midst”.
“In the midst of the assembly (בְּתוֹךְ קָהָל) I will praise you”, quoted in Heb 2:12.
“In the midst of many I will praise him.”
The man and his wife hid בְּתוֹךְ עֵץ הַגָּן, “among the trees of the garden”. The singular עֵץ names the trees collectively, and בְּתוֹךְ locates the couple among them.
Bells of gold set “in the midst of”, between, the pomegranates on the hem.
“My soul is in the midst of lions.”

senses.gloss: among, in the midst of (a company)

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, his sanctuary or his spirit set among Israel: he dwells and walks in their midst, so that their camp, land and city must be kept clean.

evidence.note: “They shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst (וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָם).”
“I will set my dwelling place in your midst … and I will walk in your midst (וְהִתְהַלַּכְתִּי בְּתוֹכְכֶם) and be your God”; quoted in 2Co 6:16.
He brought them out of Egypt “to dwell in their midst”.
The unclean are sent outside the camp, so that they do not defile the camp “in the midst of which I dwell”.
“You shall not defile the land … in the midst of which I dwell, for I, Yahweh, dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel.”
The tent of meeting “dwelling with them in the midst of their uncleanness” is covered on the day of coverings.
Korah's claim: all the congregation are holy, “and Yahweh is in their midst”.
“My spirit stands in your midst; do not fear.”
“I will set my sanctuary in their midst forever”; also 37:28, where the nations will know it.
“The place of my throne … where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever”; also 43:9.
“Behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst”, and many nations will join themselves to Yahweh.
“I will return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem.”

senses.gloss: Yahweh's dwelling in the midst of his people

senses.definition: The inside of something that encloses: a vessel, a house, a tent, a furnace, and of a man his heart and inward parts.

evidence.note: An earthen vessel that a dead creeping thing falls “into its midst (אֶל־תּוֹכוֹ)”: “all that is in its midst” is unclean.
Of the litter: its posts silver, its back gold, its seat purple, and תּוֹכוֹ, “its inside”, inlaid with love.
“My spirit faints upon me; בְּתוֹכִי, within me, my heart is desolate.”
Noah uncovered himself inside his tent.
“You shall bring her into the midst of your house.”
“As silver is melted in the midst of a furnace, so you will be melted in her midst”; also 22:18.
Wickedness thrown “into the midst of the ephah”, the lead stone on its mouth.
To the king of Tyre: “they filled your midst (תוֹכְךָ) with violence, and you sinned”.
“My heart is like wax, melted in the midst of my inward parts.”
“Your law is in the midst of my inward parts”; also 40:11, “in the midst of my heart”.
“Keep them in the midst of your heart.”

senses.definition: With מִן: from inside something, or from among a company, so taken, called or sent out of it.

evidence.note: “Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire (מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ): you heard the sound of words, but saw no form”; also 4:15; 5:4, 26.
The angel of Yahweh appeared in a flame of fire “out of the midst of the bush”; God called to Moses from it (3:4).
“I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel instead of every firstborn”; also Num 8:6.
“Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation.”
God sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow.
Twelve stones taken “out of the midst of the Jordan”.
Pharaoh: “Get out from among my people.”
Joshua did not depart from the midst of the tent.
“Go out from her midst (צְאוּ מִתּוֹכָהּ), purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of Yahweh”; quoted in 2Co 6:17.
“Flee from the midst of Babylon”; also 51:45, “Go out from her midst, my people”.
“I will bring you out of her midst and give you into the hand of strangers.”
Calves eaten “from the midst of the stall”.

senses.gloss: out of the midst of, from among (מִתּוֹךְ)

words.summary: A noun, “the middle”, found about 418 times, almost always in the construct תּוֹךְ or with a suffix (בְּתוֹכָם, מִתּוֹכָהּ) after a preposition, so that it works as one: בְּתוֹךְ “in the midst of, among”, מִתּוֹךְ “out of the midst of”, אֶל־תּוֹךְ “into”. The absolute stands with the article: בַּתָּוֶךְ “in the middle” (Gen 15:10; Num 35:5), עַמּוּדֵי הַתָּוֶךְ “the middle pillars” (Jdg 16:29). Its use is spread across the canon, and is thickest in Ezekiel and Numbers.

evidence.note: Measured מִחוּץ לָעִיר, “outside the city”, on every side, with the city בַּתָּוֶךְ.
The unclean are sent אֶל־מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה, out of the camp in whose midst Yahweh dwells.

opposites.note: Outside: what is outside the camp or city against what is in its midst.

evidence.note: Jerusalem בְּתוֹךְ הַגּוֹיִם, with lands סְבִיבוֹתֶיהָ, “all around her”.
Brightness all around the cloud, and out of its midst something like gleaming metal.

opposites.note: All around: the edge that surrounds the middle.

evidence.note: “Fifty righteous בְּתוֹךְ הָעִיר … the fifty righteous who are בְּקִרְבָּהּ.”
בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ בְּתוֹךְ הָעַמִּים, “in the midst of the earth, in the midst of the peoples”.
“Great tumults in her midst (בְּתוֹכָהּ), and the oppressed within her (בְּקִרְבָּהּ).”
The stranger who sojourns בְּתוֹכָם is cut off מִקֶּרֶב his people.

parallels.note: The inside, the midst: בְּתוֹךְ and בְּקֶרֶב stand in the two halves of one line, and say the same thing.

evidence.note: A torch בֵּין two tails, בַּתָּוֶךְ.

parallels.note: Between: the expanse is in the midst of the waters and divides between waters and waters.

phrases.gloss: in the midst of, among, within
out of the midst of, from among

evidence.note: Cedar, hyssop and scarlet thrown “into the midst of the burning of the heifer”.
The men of Ai were “in the middle” of Israel, some on this side and some on that.

phrases.gloss: dwell in the midst of (of Yahweh among his people)

senses.definition: The one in the middle of a series, between a lower or first and a higher or third.

evidence.note: The side storeys of the temple: the lowest five cubits wide, וְהַתִּיכֹנָה “and the middle” six, and the third seven.
Stairs went up to the middle storey, and from the middle to the third.
“The middle bar (הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן) in the midst of (בְּתוֹךְ) the frames”; also Exo 36:33.
Gideon came at the beginning of “the middle watch” (הָאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַתִּיכוֹנָה).
Isaiah had not yet gone out of the middle court.
The upper chambers were set back from the lower and the middle ones; also Ezk 42:5; 41:7.

words.summary: An adjective formed from תּוֹךְ: the middle one, chiefly of three in a row (storeys, watches, courts). Eleven uses, all in descriptions of buildings and times; the middle bar of the tabernacle runs בְּתוֹךְ the frames (Exo 26:28), which shows the two words side by side.
